sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, Episode 64, Cryptography.
sentences.zh: Programming Throwdown，第 64 期，密码学。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 开始吧，杰森。

sentences.en: I actually want to talk about interns and how important that is, understanding how the whole internship process works and implications there.
sentences.zh: 我其实想谈谈实习生以及这有多重要，理解整个实习流程的运作方式及其背后的意义。

sentences.en: I'll kind of walk through sort of the whole internship kind of cycle.
sentences.zh: 我大概会梳理一下整个实习的周期。

sentences.en: Basically, typically you interview, so you're typically in college, you could be undergrad, graduate student, doctoral student.
sentences.zh: 基本上，通常你会去面试，所以你一般还在上大学，可能是本科生、研究生或博士生。

sentences.en: You will interview around like December, January-ish.
sentences.zh: 你们通常会在 12 月或 1 月左右面试。

sentences.en: So you'll apply around, I guess, November, December.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你大概会在 11 月、12 月左右申请。

sentences.en: But definitely check with whatever company you're interested in because it varies.
sentences.zh: 但一定要向你感兴趣的公司确认，因为情况各不相同。

sentences.en: And then you'll do typically a couple of phone interviews.
sentences.zh: 然后通常会进行几次电话面试。

sentences.en: And then if you're accepted, you'll sort of formally accept the offer and then you'll be committed to spending your summer at whatever company you apply to.
sentences.zh: 如果被录用了，你就会正式接受Offer，然后承诺在你申请的公司度过你的夏天。

sentences.en: It's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's very sort of loose.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这相当灵活。

sentences.en: Like I've seen really amazing, super exciting internships where you're basically a full-time engineer.
sentences.zh: 比如我见过非常棒、超级令人兴奋的实习，在那里你基本上就是一名全职工程师。

sentences.en: You have a ton of responsibility.
sentences.zh: 你承担了大量的责任。

sentences.en: You have a lot of help.
sentences.zh: 你得到了很多的帮助。

sentences.en: And some amazing work comes out of it.
sentences.zh: 并从中产出了一些惊人的工作成果。

sentences.en: I've seen internships that didn't go as well.
sentences.zh: 我也见过没那么顺利的实习。

sentences.en: So because it's such a short time, there's going to be high variance, right?
sentences.zh: 所以因为时间这么短，差异性会很大，对吧？

sentences.en: But one really key thing is it's super, super important to do an internship if you want to go into industry.
sentences.zh: 但一个真正关键的点是，如果你想进入这个行业，实习真的是超级、超级重要。

sentences.en: It raises your chances of getting a job significantly.
sentences.zh: 它会显著提升你获得工作机会的几率。

sentences.en: I mean, there are times in companies I've worked at where there have been hiring freezes and they still will hire people who are interns, even through the hiring freeze.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我工作过的公司里，有时甚至在招聘冻结期间，他们仍然会雇佣实习生。

sentences.en: So it's really important.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很重要。

sentences.en: I personally haven't done an internship, but I have over the years kind of mentored interns.
sentences.zh: 我个人没有做过实习，但这些年来我指导过实习生。

sentences.en: And that's another part of it is you'll get paired up with a mentor who is kind of responsible, kind of like a manager.
sentences.zh: 这也是一部分，你会和一个导师配对，他有点像负责人，有点像经理。

sentences.en: And they're responsible for helping you, making sure that if you're blocked on something that they can get you unblocked.
sentences.zh: 他们负责帮助你，确保如果你在某事上卡壳了，他们能帮你想办法解决。

sentences.en: Of course, this is really important for an internship where you only have a couple of months.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对于只有几个月的实习来说非常重要。

sentences.en: And I think, Patrick, you actually did an internship, right?
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，我觉得你其实做过实习，对吧？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我做过。

sentences.en: I interned at a company that I ended up going to work for once I graduated because that's like a thing companies try to do is for the interns that do, you know,
sentences.zh: 我在一家公司实习过，我毕业后最终去那里工作了，因为这是公司试图做的一件事，对于那些表现好的实习生，你知道的，

sentences.en: well, they sort of already learned about them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们基本上已经了解了他们。

sentences.en: They've started, spent some money training them.
sentences.zh: 他们已经开始并在培训他们上花了一些钱。

sentences.en: And so they try to be generous in giving them offers to come work there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会慷慨地向他们提供去那里工作的Offer。

sentences.en: The other thing I don't think you mentioned is that being in engineering, specifically computer science, I've never heard of an internship that was not paid.
sentences.zh: 我觉你没有提到另一件事是，在工程领域，特别是计算机科学，我从来没听说过实习是没有薪水的。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 哦，这倒是说得好。

sentences.en: So in other sort of disciplines, it's very common to have internships that are not paid, that you sort of are expected to give work away in exchange for the experience.
sentences.zh: 所以在其他一些学科里，没有薪水的实习非常普遍，人们期望你为了经验而无偿贡献劳动。

sentences.en: But all of the programming internships I know of are paid and they're actually paid pretty well, like much better than the sort of other summer jobs I took that were internships.
sentences.zh: 但我所知道的所有编程实习都是有薪水的，而且薪水相当不错，比我做过的其他暑期实习工作要好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, internships are paid if you do some type of engineering role.
sentences.zh: 对，如果你从事某种工程类岗位，实习都是有薪的。

sentences.en: I have a friend who's in biology and their internships are not paid.
sentences.zh: 我有一个学生物的朋友，他们的实习是没有薪水的。

sentences.en: So it's kind of and they still it's still very common to do internships even in that field.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点……而且即使在那个领域，做实习仍然非常普遍。

sentences.en: So we're super lucky to be in a field where they pay interns.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常幸运能身处一个会给实习生发薪水的领域。

sentences.en: And yeah, I think it's a great experience.
sentences.zh: 而且是的，我认为这是一次极好的经历。

sentences.en: The other part of it is, you know, there's there's there's definitely a big rift, I think, between academia and industry right now.
sentences.zh: 另一部分是，你知道，现在学术界和工业界之间肯定存在着很大的鸿沟。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're in academia, you probably are being taught about linked lists and about hash tables and things like that, which are super important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你在学术界，你可能正在学习链表、哈希表之类的内容，这些都超级重要。

sentences.en: And then typically you'll have maybe one software engineering class.
sentences.zh: 然后通常你可能只有一门软件工程课。

sentences.en: But that class will at least at my university was just woefully out of date.
sentences.zh: 但那门课——至少在我所在的大学——实在是落后得令人发指。

sentences.en: You know, it's like UML diagrams or something, which is like, you know, popular in the 90s or something.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像 UML 图之类的，那可是 90 年代左右流行的东西。

sentences.en: And so, you know, getting an internship gives you just like an extraordinary experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，获得一份实习能给你带来非同寻常的经验。

sentences.en: It's very hard to sort of replicate in school.
sentences.zh: 这在学校里是很难复制的。

sentences.en: It also will help your interview skills.
sentences.zh: 它还能帮到你的面试技巧。

sentences.en: You know, it'll look it'll look good on your resume and all of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在你的简历上会很好看，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So definitely check it out if it's not on your radar.
sentences.zh: 所以如果它不在你的雷达范围内，一定要去了解一下。

sentences.en: You know, it would be good to just, you know, check out some pick your favorite companies and see sort of what they have to offer on the internship side.
sentences.zh: 你知道，选几家你最喜欢的公司，看看他们在实习方面能提供什么，这总归是好的。

sentences.en: The other part of it is it's not as big a risk for a company.
sentences.zh: 另一个部分是，对公司而言这并不是什么大风险。

sentences.en: So, you know, depending on state to state, but but in general, if if a company hires you, especially if you're there for more than three months, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这取决于不同的州，但总的来说，如果一家公司雇用了你，特别是如果你在那里呆了三个多月，你知道，

sentences.en: there's definitely it's it's hard to get rid of people to say like perfectly honestly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，要裁掉一个人绝对是很困难的。

sentences.en: It's it's hard, very hard to fire people in general.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，解雇员工是非常非常难的。

sentences.en: And I think in Europe, it's even harder.
sentences.zh: 我想在欧洲甚至更难。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what that means is people are going to be risk adverse.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着人们会趋于规避风险。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're going to take every possible precaution not to be put into an awkward position.
sentences.zh: 他们会采取一切可能的防范措施，以免让自己陷入尴尬的境地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you've done an internship that that gives extraordinary signal to that company.
sentences.zh: 如果你做过实习，那会对那家公司释放出非常强烈的信号。

sentences.en: I mean, so if it's a choice is between you and somebody else who, as far as the interview goes, is, you know, maybe even a little better, did a little better in the interview.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果选择在你和另一个人之间产生，就面试表现而言，那个人甚至可能稍微好一点，面试表现好一点。

sentences.en: But you're a sort of a sort of a short thing and they're just high variance because they didn't do an internship.
sentences.zh: 但你是一个比较稳妥的选择，而他们因为没做过实习所以变数很大。

sentences.en: I think that that will factor in right on the flip side.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会成为考量因素，没错。反过来看。

sentences.en: I don't think internships like matter to other companies to the degree that they're worth getting.
sentences.zh: 我不认为实习对其他公司有多大重要性，不值得特意去弄一个。

sentences.en: So in other words, like don't do an internship at a company that you would never work for just to do an internship.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不要仅仅为了实习而在一 家你永远不会去工作的公司实习。

sentences.en: I feel like that's a waste.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是浪费时间。

sentences.en: I think you would be better off like taking a Coursera course or something and putting that on your resume.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你还不如上个 Coursera 课程然后把它写进简历里。

sentences.en: I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'd like to hear your opinion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很想听听你的意见。

sentences.en: So I think it is absolutely true that doing an internship doesn't matter nearly as much to another company.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为绝对正确的是，做实习对另一公司而言没那么重要。

sentences.en: But even if they discount your work experience there or sort of, you know, kind of pretend that it isn't there.
sentences.zh: 但即使他们不怎么看重你在那里的工作经验，或者假装它不存在。

sentences.en: I don't think it's a negative.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是个负面因素。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: It's not they're not going to be like, oh, you did an internship at another company.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说：“哦，你在另一家公司实习过。”

sentences.en: We don't want you here.
sentences.zh: “我们不想要你。”

sentences.en: And I think there's a bunch of positives to it.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它有很多积极的方面。

sentences.en: But one, from your end, you're going to be able to have gotten a little more experience in the process of doing that, that you can talk about during your interview,
sentences.zh: 首先，从你自身角度来看，你能在实习过程中获得更多经验，你可以在面试时谈论这些，

sentences.en: that you will help you in your laSt.
sentences.zh: 这会对你的最后……

sentences.en: So typically, well, sometimes internships happen at the end of your schooling, but often they happen sort of before your final year or before your final two years.
sentences.zh: 所以通常，有时候实习发生在学业结束时，但通常它们发生在你的最后一年或最后两年之前。

sentences.en: And then it sort of gives you an opportunity to shape that last year or two years to what you learned about during your internship or what you sort of learned about the real world,
sentences.zh: 然后它让你有机会根据你在实习期间学到的东西，或者你对真实世界的了解，来塑造最后的一两年，

sentences.en: I guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜吧。

sentences.en: That sounds bad to say.
sentences.zh: 这么说听起来有点糟糕。

sentences.en: But non-academia, it's sort of what Jason was alluding to.
sentences.zh: 但非学术界，这正是杰森刚才所暗示的。

sentences.en: And I think all of those things actually help you when you go to interview.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为所有这些事情实际上在你去面试时都会帮到你。

sentences.en: People can tell, oh, this person is sort of ready.
sentences.zh: 人们能看出来，哦，这个人已经准备好了。

sentences.en: Like they sort of, they've sat here.
sentences.zh: 就像他们坐在那儿一样。

sentences.en: They're not going to ask, you're not going to have to ask questions like, what is it like to be a programmer?
sentences.zh: 你不会去问那些问题，你不需要问“程序员是什么样的”之类的问题。

sentences.en: Like, what do you do all day?
sentences.zh: 比如，“你整天都在做什么？”

sentences.en: Those might be questions that come from someone who's not.
sentences.zh: 这些可能是没做过的人才会问的问题。

sentences.en: And I think all of that sort of comes through in sort of the disposition of a person, even during interviewing, if they've done an internship before.
sentences.zh: 我想所有这些都会体现在一个人的气质中，甚至在面试时也是如此，如果他们以前做过实习的话。

sentences.en: I mean, taking a Coursera course is great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，上 Coursera 课程当然很好。

sentences.en: I don't know how to really compare and contrast those.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么真正比较和对比这些。

sentences.en: But I think there is value.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这确实有价值。

sentences.en: I mean, at some point, taking it in sort of a field of computer science you're not interested in going into and at a company that's not very reputable or whatever,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时候，即使是在你不想从事的计算机科学领域，在一家名气不大的公司实习，

sentences.en: at least you still get paid.
sentences.zh: 至少你还能拿工资。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 所以也有这个好处。

sentences.en: And like making money is sort of good to like help you get through college.
sentences.zh: 而且赚钱对帮自己度过大学生活挺有帮助的。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: Because that was sort of broken college.
sentences.zh: 因为大学挺缺钱的。

sentences.en: Yeah, same here.
sentences.zh: 对，我也是。

sentences.en: So that was really nice.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很棒。

sentences.en: And I see what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's fair.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这倒也是。

sentences.en: But I wouldn't say, it's a case-by-case basis.
sentences.zh: 但我不会一概而论，这得具体情况具体分析。

sentences.en: You sort of have to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 你必须做出决定。

sentences.en: But I do actually think there's enormous value.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这具有巨大的价值。

sentences.en: In my time when I was back at college after doing an internship, it gave me, I feel, a much different view on my professors and what they were saying,
sentences.zh: 我在实习结束后回到大学的那段时光里，我觉得它让我对教授和他们所说的话有了截然不同的看法，

sentences.en: where it allowed me to sort of apply what was being said a little more intelligently and sort of focus on the parts that I really wanted to make sure I knew.
sentences.zh: 它让我能够更聪明地应用所讲的内容，并专注于我真正想要确保自己掌握的部分。

sentences.en: And sort of, in my mind, since I wasn't going in academia,
sentences.zh: 并且在我脑海里，既然我不打算走学术路线，

sentences.en: it allowed me to discount some of the stuff that I realized was sort of no longer applicable to kind of the stuff I would need when I first came out of the gate.
sentences.zh: 它让我得以忽略掉那些我意识到已经不再适用于我刚步入职场时所需技能的东西。

sentences.en: It makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这倒说得通。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm definitely kind of like a bookworm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我绝对是个书呆子。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a bit of like, I think my value is coming out.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这有点像，我觉得我的价值正在显现。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think, so maybe, I mean, one thing I think we both agree on is definitely, you know, take the time to like intern,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我认为，所以也许，我的意思是，有一点我们两个都同意，那就是一定要花时间去实习，

sentences.en: to take the time to pick a company for your internship that you would want to work for.
sentences.zh: 花时间为你的实习选择一家你想为其工作的公司。

sentences.en: Like that, like, like interning, you know, gives you a huge leg up at that company that you interned at.
sentences.zh: 就像实习会为你在这家实习公司带来巨大的优势一样。

sentences.en: And so don't kind of like waste that.
sentences.zh: 所以不要浪费这个机会。

sentences.en: Like if you really want to work at, you know, General Electric or something, then do an internship there.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想去通用电气之类的公司工作，那就去那里实习。

sentences.en: And what that means is kind of really doing research kind of early on the companies and, you know, where you want to work.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要很早就开始对公司以及你想在哪里工作进行研究。

sentences.en: But yeah, I see your point that there's definitely, you get a ton of experience either way.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我明白你的意思，无论如何你都能获得大量的经验。

sentences.en: And I think you're right that even if,
sentences.zh: 而且我想你是对的，即使，

sentences.en: let's say you do internship at GE and then you go interview somewhere else and they don't really know much about GE or care or something like that,
sentences.zh: 假设你在通用电气实习，然后你去别的地方面试，而他们对通用电气了解不多或者根本不在乎，

sentences.en: you're still going to have experience that's going to show that you would have had otherwise.
sentences.zh: 你仍然会拥有本来不会有的经验。

sentences.en: All right, time for news.
sentences.zh: 好了，新闻时间。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so this is, this is one of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，所以这是，这是其中一件事。

sentences.en: It's almost like scary to even bring up, but we have to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 甚至提起来都让人觉得有点害怕，但我们必须谈谈它。

sentences.en: They're listening.
sentences.zh: 他们在听呢。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So, so I'm sure everyone's seen by now this whole Vault 7 WikiLeaks thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以我相信大家现在都已经看到维基解密关于“七号保险库”（Vault 7）的这个事情了。

sentences.en: Basically, and I guess, I mean, I don't know if it's, I mean, I don't know how much of it has been sort of proven or not.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我猜，我的意思是，我不知道这是否，我的意思是，我不知道其中有多少已经被证实了。

sentences.en: I haven't been following it too closely, I have to admit.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我没有太密切地关注它。

sentences.en: But basically, WikiLeaks released a bunch of documents from the CIA and among other things, it says that if you had a Samsung smart TV,
sentences.zh: 但基本上，维基解密发布了一堆来自中情局的文件，其中提到如果你有一台三星智能电视，

sentences.en: that they had some sort of hack where from your Wi-Fi router, they could like get into your Wi-Fi router.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种黑客攻击手段，可以通过你的 Wi-Fi 路由器侵入进去。

sentences.en: And then from there, they could get into your TV and they could actually turn on the microphone just at will.
sentences.zh: 然后从那里，他们可以进入你的电视，甚至可以随心所欲地打开麦克风。

sentences.en: So, and so presumably they were just turning on the microphone, they're collecting all of this audio, and then they were shipping it to Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以大概他们只是打开麦克风，收集所有这些音频，然后将其运送到德国。

sentences.en: Because I guess the idea was that if they get caught, then they can like say that it was the Germans who were doing it.
sentences.zh: 因为我想他们的想法是，如果被抓住了，他们就可以说是德国人干的。

sentences.en: So it's sort of like a way to cover their tracks.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是掩人耳目的方式。

sentences.en: But I guess apparently there's like, and again, this is all from the WikiLeaks.
sentences.zh: 但我想显然有，而且再次说明，这些都来自维基解密。

sentences.en: I don't know if any of it is true.
sentences.zh: 我不知道其中是否有任何真实性。

sentences.en: I'm not going to, I have no idea, right?
sentences.zh: 我不会去，我完全不知道，对吧？

sentences.en: But, but according to this report, there's a bunch of Americans, you know, living in Europe, doing like all this analysis on all of this illegally collected data.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是根据这份报告，有一群美国人，你知道，住在欧洲，在对所有这些非法收集的数据进行各种分析。

sentences.en: And, you know, presumably they're like looking for people who are like speaking a certain way or saying dangerous things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，大概他们在寻找那些以某种特定方式说话或说危险话语的人。

sentences.en: I don't know, but, but the whole thing is crazy.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但是，整件事太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, it goes way beyond Samsung Tvs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这远不止三星电视那么简单。

sentences.en: It's like iPhones.
sentences.zh: 这就好比iPhone。

sentences.en: There's like zero day exploits for iPhones that, that, that they had, that they weren't giving to anyone so that they could like survey people on their iPhone.

sentences.en: You know, my, my ignorance of the topic is kind of showing through.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我对这个话题的无知有点暴露无遗了。

sentences.zh: 我看到了最初的新闻报道，我把它贴在这里了。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, there's a ton of information.

sentences.zh: 你大概不想把这东西放在工作电脑上。

sentences.en: Um, um, that's one of these things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，这就是其中之一。

sentences.en: It's like, you don't really think about, cause it's not really illegal.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你平时不会多想，因为这其实并不违法。

sentences.en: It's not like pornography or something like that, but I just, I just, I don't know, maybe it's just me being paranoid,
sentences.zh: 它不像色情内容之类的那样，但我只是，我只是，不知道，也许是我自己被迫害妄想吧，

sentences.en: but I feel like this is probably not something that you want on your work computer.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这大概不是你想放在工作电脑上的东西。

sentences.en: Um, um, but yeah, I mean, you know, when you have time, at least read the articles, uh, it's, it's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，不过说真的，你知道的，有空的时候至少读读那些文章，呃，真的非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: I mean, even if it's not true, just the, the, like the whole story just seems completely plausible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使这不是真的，光是整个故事听起来也完全合情合理。

sentences.en: And, uh, yeah, I mean, it's, it's, it's an amazing read.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，是的，我是说，这绝对是一本极佳的读物。

sentences.en: There's also tools.
sentences.zh: 里面还有各种工具。

sentences.en: You can actually download these like windows and Linux tools that supposedly let you, I don't know, sniff ports or something.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以下载这些Windows和Linux工具，它们据说能让你，我不知道，嗅探端口之类的。

sentences.en: I don't know too much about it, but they have the source code and everything, which is kind of wild.
sentences.zh: 我对这个了解不多，但它们连源代码都有，这真是有点疯狂。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, as you said, even if it is sort of fabricated that it was the CIA or the CIA was behind that or not fabricated, but whatever miscommunicated, misunderstood, who knows,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如你所说，即使这事有点虚构，比如是中情局干的或是中情局在背后主使，或者并非虚构，而是传达错误、产生误解，谁知道呢，

sentences.en: even if that part isn't correct, then, um, it, it gets people thinking about all these sort of internet of things, the smart TVs, the smart toasters, the smart microwave, you know,
sentences.zh: 退一步讲，即使那部分不属实，那也，呃，它会引发人们对所有这些物联网设备的思考，智能电视、智能烤面包机、智能微波炉，你知道的，

sentences.en: anytime they put a microphone on there to listen to you for some reason, you know,
sentences.zh: 任何时候，只要它们出于某种原因在设备上装了麦克风来监听你，你知道的，

sentences.en: even a sort of legitimate reason, then someone could figure out a way to tap into that and gather that data.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是出于某种合理的理由，别人也能想出办法来接入并收集这些数据。

sentences.en: Even if the company is complicit or non-complicit with that.
sentences.zh: 不管这家公司是否与此串通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I, you know, I had friends, uh, uh, you know, coworkers who, uh, you know, would put tape over their laptop camera and, uh, tape over their microphone.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我，你知道的，我有朋友，呃，你知道的，有些同事会用胶带把笔记本电脑的摄像头和麦克风封起来。

sentences.en: And I kind of like, I mean, I didn't think they were kind of like tinfoil hat wearers or something like that.
sentences.zh: 而我有点，我的意思是，我并不觉得他们是什么戴着锡纸帽的阴谋论者之类的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like, you know, makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得，你知道的，这挺合情合理的。

sentences.en: Maybe you have an accident and you turn it on when you're not supposed to, or, or like, you know, maybe you actually download a virus,
sentences.zh: 也许你会不小心在不该开启的时候把它打开，或者，你知道的，也许你真的下载了病毒，

sentences.en: like you install some program that's malware or something.
sentences.zh: 比如你安装了某些带有恶意软件的程序之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, but I thought the idea of like, Oh, the government has some zero day exploit in the OS and they could just, you know, turn on your camera.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我原以为那种“政府在操作系统里藏了零日漏洞，然后就能直接开启你的摄像头”的说法，

sentences.en: I will, I thought that was kind of like a stretch, like kind of out there.
sentences.zh: 我原以为那有点夸大其词，有点离谱了。

sentences.en: Um, but yeah, after this report, uh, I believe it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过说实话，看完这份报告后，我信了。

sentences.en: I mean, I still haven't taped over my camera.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我还是没用胶带封住摄像头。

sentences.en: Maybe I just don't care if someone's watching me.
sentences.zh: 也许我只是不在乎有没有人在监视我吧。

sentences.en: Um, but, but yeah, I totally think that I could be watched at any time, which is, which is, which is kind of strange.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过，真的，我完全觉得我随时可能会被监视，这感觉，这感觉，这感觉有点诡异。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Oh, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 哦，请说。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: This sounds really silly, but you said put tape over the camera.
sentences.zh: 这听起来真的很傻，但你刚才说用胶带封住摄像头。

sentences.en: And I have actually done that a couple of times because we used to have a video conferencing tool that had the option of having video on or off.
sentences.zh: 我其实真的这么做过好几次，因为我们以前用过一个视频会议工具，它有开启或关闭视频的选项。

sentences.en: And sometimes you would sort of not be paying attention or not have the configuration right.
sentences.zh: 有时你可能没怎么注意，或者配置没弄好。

sentences.en: And it would turn on the video by default.
sentences.zh: 它就会默认把视频打开。

sentences.en: And then until you sort of realized it and turned it off, people would see you sort of, you know, no, no, not doing something weird.
sentences.zh: 然后直到你意识到并把它关掉之前，大家都会看到你，你知道的，没，没在做什么奇怪的事，

sentences.en: It's just a sort of catch you off guard.
sentences.zh: 就是有点杀你个措手不及。

sentences.en: And so I actually did have something over it.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的在上面贴了东西。

sentences.en: When I don't think people are watching, I like scratch my face.
sentences.zh: 当我觉得没人看着的时候，我喜欢挠挠脸。

sentences.en: Like, you know, you just do these like ritual things.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，你就是会做这些习惯性的动作。

sentences.en: And yeah, I mean, it's kind of embarrassing, right?
sentences.zh: 然后，是的，这挺尴尬的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so I put electrical tape over it, like some opaque tape that you couldn't see through.
sentences.zh: 所以我上面贴了电工胶带，就是那种看不透的不透明胶带。

sentences.en: Because I thought that made sense.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这样很合理。

sentences.en: And then someone the other day had cellophane tape, like clear scotch tape.
sentences.zh: 然后前几天有人用的是透明胶带，就是那种普通的透明胶纸。

sentences.en: You know, it's like sort of hazy over theirs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，贴在上面雾蒙蒙的。

sentences.en: And I didn't get it at firSt.
sentences.zh: 我一开始没明白。

sentences.en: And then I like realized and then asked them to confirm that this is why it's sort of one.
sentences.zh: 然后我反应过来了，还向他们确认这就是这么贴的原因。

sentences.en: It wasn't as tacky because it wasn't as obvious to the when you looked at it.
sentences.zh: 它没那么显眼，因为看上去不那么明显。

sentences.en: Also, the some of the computers use the camera to do ambient light sensing or in that area to do ambient light sensing.
sentences.zh: 另外，有些电脑会利用摄像头进行环境光感测，或者在那个区域进行环境光感测。

sentences.en: And if you tape over it with tape, you ruin that or like electrical tape or a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 如果你用胶带把它封死，就会破坏这个功能，比如用电工胶带或一张纸。

sentences.en: But if you put the cellophane tape, it can still sense the light.
sentences.zh: 但如果你贴的是透明胶带，它依然能感应到光线。

sentences.en: But everything is sort of too blurry.
sentences.zh: 只不过所有东西看上去都太模糊了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这倒挺合理。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, I guess that seems silly.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，噢，这听起来好像挺傻的。

sentences.en: But to me, I was just like, wow, that's really smart.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，我只想说，哇，这真的太聪明了。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全赞同。

sentences.en: So if you don't want to go all the way in use.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不想做得那么彻底的话。

sentences.en: We're going to see a lot of this now, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我们以后会看到很多这样的产品。

sentences.en: You know, like we're going to see a whole market of smartphone cases that can, you know, cover and uncover the camera.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们将会看到整个市场上出现各种智能手机壳，它们能盖住和遮挡摄像头。

sentences.en: I just feel like this is like a thing that's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这会成为一种趋势。

sentences.en: I feel the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我的看法恰好相反。

sentences.en: I feel like people are scarily desensitized and not caring about this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们已经麻木到了可怕的地步，根本不在乎这个。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you'd be right in the case of me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，如果拿我作例子的话，你说得对。

sentences.en: I don't really care enough.
sentences.zh: 我其实没那么在乎。

sentences.en: And maybe that's a scary thing.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是可怕的地方吧。

sentences.en: But no, I think that, you know, even if 1% of the people care enough, that's enough of a market for someone to make a case with a lid or something.
sentences.zh: 不过不，我觉得，你知道的，哪怕只有1%的人足够在乎，这也足够撑起一个市场，让别人去生产带滑盖之类的手机壳了。

sentences.en: I'm not denying cases will be made.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说不会有人生产这种手机壳。

sentences.en: I'm just denying that they're going to get used.
sentences.zh: 我只是说没人会去用它们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 对，我同意这一点。

sentences.en: Well, my news article is about Shaw 1 collision.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的新闻报道是关于SHA-1碰撞的。

sentences.en: So I guess this is from Google announced they, I guess they were trying to call it something cool.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这是来自谷歌发布的公告，我想他们当时想给它起个酷一点的名字。

sentences.en: They called it shattered.
sentences.zh: 他们把它叫做“破碎”（shattered）。

sentences.en: So they named the bug.
sentences.zh: 所以他们给这个漏洞取了名字。

sentences.en: It's not really a bug, but there's a tradition of naming, I guess, exploits and bugs.
sentences.zh: 它其实算不上一个漏洞，但给漏洞和攻击命名似乎是个传统。

sentences.en: So they named it shattered.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把它命名为“破碎”。

sentences.en: But what it really is, is Shaw 1, which is a way of hashing the data,
sentences.zh: 但它实际上的原理是SHA-1，这是一种对数据进行哈希处理的方法，

sentences.en: which means you sort of take a document or a bit of data and you run it byte by byte or sets of bytes by sets of bytes through an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你拿出一份文档或一串数据，然后让它字节对字节地，或者按字节组通过一个算法。

sentences.en: And you get some, it's called a hash back.
sentences.zh: 然后你会得到一些东西，被称为哈希值。

sentences.en: It's some representation of that data so that if you make any change to the data, it is statistically improbable that the hash is the same for two different inputs.
sentences.zh: 它是该数据的一种表现形式，因此如果你对数据做任何改动，两个不同的输入产生相同哈希值的概率在统计学上是微乎其微的。

sentences.en: Now, of course, if your hash is smaller than your input, it's always possible.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你的哈希值比输入的数据短，那这种事总是可能的。

sentences.en: So if you have an input that's 256 bytes and you use only one byte hash, then, of course, there's always a chance that they'll have a collision.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个256字节的输入，却只用一个字节的哈希值，那么，当然，它们总是有可能会发生碰撞。

sentences.en: But with a big enough hash, the chance of collision goes down dramatically.
sentences.zh: 但只要哈希值足够大，发生碰撞的概率就会急剧下降。

sentences.en: You could imagine for 256, a one byte number, a 256 combinations that any two documents have, what would that be?
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下，对于256来说，一个字节的数字，任意两个文档会有256种组合，那会是什么样？

sentences.en: One in 256 chance of collision.
sentences.zh: 有256分之一的碰撞几率。

sentences.en: And then there's sort of the, what do they call it, the birthday problem, where there's sort of a little bit of unintuitiveness if you're not used to dealing with it,
sentences.zh: 然后还有那种，他们叫什么来着，生日悖论，如果你不常接触的话，会觉得有点违反直觉，

sentences.en: where your chance of collision goes up more quickly than you would otherwise sort of think.
sentences.zh: 也就是碰撞发生的概率比你想象的要上升得更快。

sentences.en: But even with that, that with the longer hashes, it sort of was for a long time unreasonable to expect that there would be a collision,
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，随着哈希值变长，在很长一段时间里，人们都认为不可能出现碰撞，

sentences.en: which is two different inputs causing the same result.
sentences.zh: 也就是两个不同的输入产生相同的结果。

sentences.en: And the reason why that's bad is if you imagine someone is, like when you see the sort of hash codes for downloads, when you download, especially like security tools,
sentences.zh: 而这之所以糟糕是因为，如果你想象有人在做一件事，就像你看到下载内容的哈希码时那样，当你下载东西时，特别是像安全工具，

sentences.en: like an SSH tool, and you'll see like, oh, here's the hash.
sentences.zh: 比如SSH工具，你会看到类似“哦，这是哈希值”。

sentences.en: And you're supposed to hash it on your computer to make sure that the thing you download matches the thing the author intended to.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要在你的电脑上对它进行哈希计算，以确保你下载的东西与作者的初衷完全一致。

sentences.en: And so that way, you know, nobody's changed it.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，你就知道没有人篡改过它。

sentences.en: And with a collision, they could give you a virus instead of an SSH tool.
sentences.zh: 而如果存在碰撞，他们就可以用病毒来替代SSH工具发给你。

sentences.en: And so what Google did here was created two different PDFs.
sentences.zh: 所以谷歌这次做的是创建了两个不同的PDF文件。

sentences.en: And I haven't actually opened the PDFs, but I read that they were essentially two images.
sentences.zh: 我其实并没有打开过这两个PDF，但我读到过它们本质上是两张图片。

sentences.en: So on the first PDF, there's an image.
sentences.zh: 在第一个PDF里，有一张图片。

sentences.en: On the second PDF, there's a completely different image.
sentences.zh: 在第二个PDF里，是一张完全不同的图片。

sentences.en: They don't resemble each other at all.
sentences.zh: 它们长得一点都不像。

sentences.en: But if you run them through this SHA-1 algorithm for generating a hash, the hash will be identical.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它们通过这个用于生成哈希值的SHA-1算法，它们的哈希值将完全相同。

sentences.en: And what they did it on purpose.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是故意这么做的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They found two different documents that collided.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了两个会产生碰撞的不同文档。

sentences.en: And the important thing is that because you could generate just random data and hash it, and then generate more random data and hash it, and eventually you'll get a collision,
sentences.zh: 重要的一点是，因为你可以生成随机数据并对其进行哈希，然后生成更多随机数据并对其哈希，最终你会得到一个碰撞，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But in this case, they can actually manipulate the collision.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他们实际上可以人为操纵这个碰撞。

sentences.en: So in other words, like they can get something, not just random, but something they want to collide with something else.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们能搞出一些东西，不只是随机的，而是他们希望与另一个东西发生碰撞的东西。

sentences.en: And that's where it gets kind of dangerous, right?
sentences.zh: 而这正是危险所在，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyway, and a funny kind of side note on this, they put into Chrome a unit test where there was a collision.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，关于这件事还有一个挺有意思的小插曲，他们在Chromium里加入了一个会产生碰撞的单元测试。

sentences.en: And so just as part of Chromium, and I guess Chromium, like, I actually don't know why they put it as a unit teSt.
sentences.zh: 作为Chromium的一部分，我其实不知道他们为什么要把它设为单元测试。

sentences.en: Maybe it's just to remind people never to use SHA-1.
sentences.zh: 也许只是为了提醒大家永远不要使用SHA-1。

sentences.en: But as soon as they put in that unit test, and they put in those two PDF files, it actually broke a Git.
sentences.zh: 但就在他们加入这个单元测试并放入那两个PDF文件后，它竟然把Git弄崩溃了。
